title: Reduce prefill CPU overhead via SIMD-aware token bucketing and adaptive decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
The prefill side (prompt/token preprocessing) is a dominant CPU cost on many customer workloads, especially for high-throughput, short-turnaround requests. We observe: high per-request normalization overhead for ASCII vs multi-byte UTF-8, costly branch-heavy codepaths for small inputs, and inefficient scheduling that results in cache churn and increased decode latency tail.

Goals:
- Reduce CPU cycles spent in tokenization/normalization by 25–40% for typical PLG workloads (short prompts, ASCII-heavy).
- Maintain or improve p50/p95 prefill latency; avoid increasing tail latency for long inputs.
- Provide runtime knobs to route requests to different preprocessing kernels and to adapt decode scheduling based on workload shape.

Proposal (high level):
1) SIMD-aware token bucketing: on ingress, classify requests into buckets (ASCII-fast, mixed-utf8, wide-codepoint). Route ASCII-fast to a narrow, vectorized normalization+split kernel implemented with explicit SIMD intrinsics (AVX2/AVX512 fallback paths). Mixed/wide inputs flow to the conservative scalar pipeline.

2) Per-core micro-batching via token buckets: maintain small-per-core request buckets to coalesce normalization work for many tiny requests (<= 64 bytes). This reduces syscall/context-switching overhead and enables amortized vectorization. Buckets flush on size/time thresholds to preserve latency SLOs.

3) Adaptive decode scheduling hints: annotate prefill output with a compact kernel_hint (token_count_category + bucket_type). The decode scheduler uses kernel_hint to pick the most suitable attention kernel (low-latency vs high-throughput) and to place the decode task on cores with warm KV cache affinity.

4) Fallback and safety: correctness-first scalar path and sanitizers for multibyte sequences, with runtime flags to disable SIMD path for compatibility/bug triage. Feature-flagged rollout with per-customer opt-in.

Design tradeoffs and rationale:
- Complexity vs gain: SIMD kernels add maintenance burden but provide large wins on common ASCII workloads. We minimize scope by targeting only the ASCII-fast kernel and keeping other paths unchanged.
- Latency vs throughput: micro-batching improves throughput but risks increasing p95. We will implement adaptive flush thresholds and per-customer SLO knobs to control batching aggressiveness.
- Portability: provide multi-platform code paths (x86 AVX2/512 and a scalar fallback). Consider later Neon implementation for ARM64 cloud regions.

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Throughput (tokens/sec) improvement on ASCII-heavy benchmark >= 2.0x and on mixed workloads >= 1.25x.
- CPU-seconds per 1M tokens reduced by >= 25% on target workloads.
- Prefill p95 increase <= 5ms for short prompts; no regression for long prompts.
- No functional tokenization/regression test failures across model suite.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike (2w): microbenchmark SIMD normalization on representative corpora; verify correctness across multi-byte edge cases. Produce baseline numbers and microkernel prototype. (owner: Miguel)
- Prototype integration (2w): wire bucket classifier into prefill ingress, implement per-core micro-bucket, add kernel_hint to prefill output. Feature-flag on. (owner: Miguel)
- End-to-end perf tests (1w): run e2e workloads on staging, measure tokens/sec, p50/p95 prefill latency, CPU usage. Tune flush thresholds. (owner: Aisha)
- Code review and security review (1w): include sanitizers, integer overflow checks, and a brief threat assessment for malformed inputs. (owner: Security)
- Canary rollout (2w): enable for 10% of internal production traffic with detailed telemetry dashboards. Monitor decode kernel selection distribution and tail latencies. (owner: SRE)
- GA and docs (1w): document knobs, rollout guide, and how to disable per-customer. (owner: Docs)

Dependencies:
["ENG-314159","ENG-631482","ENG-42111"]

Risks and mitigations:
- SIMD correctness edge cases (zero-width joiners, combining marks): test corpus expanded and fuzz tester added; scalar fallback if sanitizer triggers.
- Increased GC or memory pressure from per-core buckets: enforce fixed-size buckets and backpressure to ingress layer.
- Unexpected p95 regressions: adaptive flush and immediate disable flag for emergency rollback.

Rollout and observability:
- New telemetry: prefill.kernel_bucket, prefill.path (simd|scalar), prefill.bucket_flush_latency, decode.kernel_selected, prefill.cpu_ms.
- Dashboards: per-customer breakdown and per-region telemetry; alert if p95 prefill increases > 10% for a customer.

comments: 2025-02-10 - Triage: Logged after profiling session — prefill accounted for ~42% of CPU on small prompt workload (internal sim).
2025-02-17 - Spike complete: SIMD prototype (AVX2) shows 2.3x tokens/sec on ascii-heavy microbench; mixed workload 1.15x. Found edge-case with U+200D sequences; added sanitizer to scalar fallback.

2025-02-24 - Prototype integration: per-core buckets implemented; initial staging run indicates 30% CPU reduction and small p95 regressions for 3% of traffic. Tuning flush thresholds reduced regressions.
2025-03-01 - Perf run: tokens/sec improved 2.0x on target PLG mix, CPU-seconds/1M tokens down 33%. Preparing canary rollout + docs.
